turns.userMessage: I organise our team's thank-you lunches and usually pay the deposit myself. Everyone says how appreciated I am, but lately the thanks feel oddly like being handed my own effort back. Can you help me separate wanting recognition from wanting somebody else to carry a bit of the work?
turns.reply:
Those may be two different needs, and it can be both. Recognition is about your effort being noticed in a way that feels specific and real to you. Shared work is about someone else taking responsibility for a piece of the lunch—perhaps planning, booking, or covering the deposit—rather than only appreciating that you did it.

A small thought experiment might help separate them: if the work stayed exactly the same but people thanked you in a way that felt more meaningful, would that ease the feeling? And, separately, if someone took a concrete part of the work but offered little extra praise, would that ease it? Your reactions to each can help show what you’re wanting most right now.
